assessments.reasoning: SQLite’s language guide describes the SQL accepted by the implementation and explicitly identifies both omissions from standard SQL and additions of its own. That supports the dialect identity. The guide gives a general description, while the companion release notes anchor specific SQL changes to 3.46.0. The active designation belongs to the catalog.

SQLite’s 3.46.0 release notes document two directly visible changes to SQL that a user can write. A numeric literal can contain an underscore between digits, and SQL expressions gain the json_pretty function. These examples establish the release-specific clause. The language guide supplies the general account of omissions and additions, without requiring either release example to be classified against an ISO edition.
